The GrowthCred field guide

Stop risky copy-pasting with a POPIA-safe AI policy and staff training checklist.

A busy person pasting an ID number or a client file into a chat box is more common than a dramatic hack. That is a POPIA question.

A short rule your staff can repeat, plus live practice on stripped work, is how you stay careful.

Quick answer

It does make you responsible for personal information. A person still checks the draft.

4 min read

You'll learn

  1. You get five short rules your staff can repeat on a busy afternoon.
  2. You see how to run the checklist and a live session before you open the chat tools.

Why listen to GrowthCred

GrowthCred is a Johannesburg AI implementation and training company. I teach AI at Melsoft Academy. I helped build an isiZulu and English speech AI system. It was presented at Parliament in Cape Town.

1Chat boxes are not private filing cabinets

The problem

  1. Your staff treat a browser chat box like a private scratchpad. They paste names, ID numbers, phone numbers, addresses, bank details or client files.
  2. A paid plan does not settle where your text goes. A wrong summary, even with no personal data, can still land on someone's file.

The way through

  1. You check the terms of the account your staff actually use. You ban raw personal information in a tool you have not approved.
  2. You have a person check every draft before it is sent, filed or acted on.

A chat box is not a scratchpad. A client file is not a test prompt.

2Short spoken rules beat a long policy on a shared drive

The problem

  1. A policy on a shared drive rarely stops your people when they are rushing a deadline.
  2. If your rule is not plain, your staff guess. Or they use a personal login.

The way through

  1. You keep five habits they can say in one breath. No raw personal data in an unapproved tool. Use a stripped or made-up example when that is enough. Stick to the approved account. Check every draft. If you are unsure, stop and ask.
  2. Your staff stop and ask when they are unsure. They do not improvise.

If your staff cannot repeat the rule on a busy afternoon, it will not hold.

3A twelve-point checklist sets the ground rules first

The problem

  1. If you tell staff the chat is allowed before you name the owner, the tools, the forbidden data and the sign-off, you leave blind spots.
  2. If you skip the review points, a bad summary, or a stale rule, stays in place.

The way through

  1. You work through the twelve items before you allow the chat for everyday work.
  2. This is your working list. It is not a downloadable policy, and it is not a legal opinion.

Run the checklist before you allow the chat box for everyday work.

  • You name who owns the AI rule.
  • You write the rule in words a busy person can repeat.
  • You name the tools that are allowed. You name the ones that are not.
  • You say what must never be pasted in.
  • You name who signs the draft.
  • You find who is already using a chat box.
  • You train live, on real tasks, in Johannesburg or online.
  • You practise stripping names before you draft.
  • You practise checking the draft against the source.
  • You give staff one way to ask when they are unsure.
  • You look again after the first month.
  • You update the rule when the tool or the work changes.

4Live practice teaches staff to strip a file before they draft

The problem

  1. Under a deadline, your people take the fastest path. If they have never practised stripping a file, they paste the raw one.
  2. Your managers miss an invented line, or a slip in tone, if they have not practised checking a draft against the source.

The way through

  1. You practise together in a live session, in Johannesburg or online. You rewrite one request so the structure comes back without the sensitive detail.
  2. You spot the invented line in the room. You show managers how to review the draft. Final sign-off stays with a person.

Your staff will paste the whole file under pressure unless you practise stripping it first.

5Know what this checklist and this training do not cover

The problem

  1. A checklist or a training session is not legal POPIA compliance. Treating it as one is false confidence.
  2. Practical training is not an accredited qualification. It is also not a lending service.

The way through

  1. Your Information Officer and a lawyer review your own facts and policies. This page is not legal advice. Training does not make you compliant.
  2. GrowthCred (Pty) Ltd, in Rosebank, provides practical training. It is not an accredited qualification. We are not Growth Credit Ltd. We do not lend money.

Practical training builds safer habits. Your Information Officer and your lawyer own the legal question.

Want the team to practise stripping examples and checking drafts together? Ask for a quote for a live session in Johannesburg or online. We use your real tasks and the confidentiality rule you already have. You do not get a canned template you still have to adapt.

This page is practical guidance, not legal advice. You can start the working checklist before a formal sign-off. Your Information Officer and your lawyer should still review your facts before you roll it out.

Frequently asked questions

Does POPIA ban staff from using AI?+
No. POPIA does not ban AI. It does make you responsible for personal information. Your staff should not paste names, ID numbers or client files into an unapproved public chat. You still have a person check the draft.
Does this page give a downloadable POPIA policy or a legal compliance guarantee?+
No. This page is not legal advice. It does not publish a downloadable policy. Training does not make a workflow POPIA-compliant. Your Information Officer and your lawyer must review your facts.
